description: Locally frozen OMS submission snapshot for "Pre-Export Row Scaling for Generated Mixed-Integer Programs: Accuracy Contracts and Software Evaluation", supplied as Supplementary Material 2. This metadata prepares a later deposition; it does not assign a DOI or assert journal submission, acceptance or publication. The historical baseline v1.2-coap-submission is archived separately at 10.5281/zenodo.23145294. The snapshot contains the C++ generator, Python residual-budget selector, native integration, source models, contracts, unit conversions, native logs, stored points, exact witnesses and independent replay programs. Evaluation includes the 306-model fixed-basis audit, kernel-matched and Ruiz controls, operational reconstruction, three-solver enumerated stress tests, activation studies, independent batch-scheduling transfer, integer-tolerance controls and complete-process measurements. The v1.3.15 study supplies the previously omitted unscaled control of the favorable dispatch experiment: 36 matched Base/Base-tight calls and a conditional 54-call contemporaneous interleaved repeat, on six known models and three seeds. At 100 m3, Budget-L2/Base and Budget-L2/Base-tight geometric work ratios are 0.317 and 0.264. All policies meet the tested primal budgets without detected bound/completion contradictions; maximum candidate-cost worsening is below 0.1%. Interleaved complete-process time ratios are 0.621 and 0.570 on the shared host, while the three inexpensive models are slower. All 54 native endpoints and points repeat exactly. This supports within-family effort benefits, not additional primal recovery over Base, external generalization or equally certified MILP gaps. The complete sensitivity retains abstentions and adverse results. Batch scheduling verifies budget delivery without additional primal benefit over matched L2. The exact Supplementary Material 1 PDF is included. Saved-result replay needs no commercial solver license. Only reconstruction of all 1,530 historical bases additionally requires the separate baseline bulk archive. Code: MIT; data/results: CC BY 4.0; manuscript outside those licenses. No external financial funding or research grant was received; historical ClusterUY computing resources are acknowledged. The v1.3.16–v1.3.17 editorial closure adds no optimizer calls: it makes paired geometric means explicit, exposes per-model complete-process time in the main article, and includes the clean-extraction replay report and guide in the complete delivery.
